comments.text: Finance asked whether we can use a semicolon as separator, their spreadsheet locale expects it. Let's do semicolon.
Noted. @Mira Castell do we also need the invoice lines, or only one row per invoice?

One row per invoice. Lines are a separate story if Finance ever needs them.
What should happen for very large exports? Production has roughly 180k invoices.
Cap it at 10,000 rows. Finance always filters by month; if more match, return an error that tells them to narrow the filter.
QA note: I will test with customer names containing commas and quotes. The seed data has Eskholt Interiors, Ltd. and Grisdale "Old Mill" Brewing.
Update after talking to Finance again: the semicolon is not needed, plain comma is fine. Their spreadsheet import handles RFC 4180 CSV.
The export button comes with the UI refresh feature. Nothing needed in src/frontend for this story.
Filename will be invoices-yyyyMMdd.csv from the injected TimeProvider, not DateTime.Now (coding standards).
Reminder: the export contains customer data. It stays behind the same access rules as the invoice list and is never written to shared folders.
QA plan ready: filters, date range inclusive on both ends, 422 above 10,000 rows, quoting of commas, quotes and newlines. @Dana Novak ping me when the branch is pushed.
